title: How well do LLMs understand code?
task: Benchmarking large language model understanding of code semantics
key_results: Best model achieved 80.42% accuracy on semantic questions (15,404 questions across 1000 C programs); failure rates range 19.58-86.01% across models; function reachability shows strongest correlation with code-generation benchmarks
comments: SemBench is a valuable diagnostic benchmark revealing a systematic gap between generation and comprehension; however, semantic understanding may not fully explain generation quality, as models might use statistical patterns without explicit reasoning.

inputs: Semantic question sets (n=15,404) covering dead code, data dependency, function reachability, dominators, liveness
outputs: Accuracy per model and semantic category
Correlation with HumanEval and MBPP code-generation benchmarks

hypotheses.hypothesis: LLMs understand code semantics at the same level as code generation capability
hypotheses.result: Rejected; substantial gap observed (best accuracy 80.42% vs. strong generation performance)

hypotheses.hypothesis: Specific semantic abilities (e.g., function reachability) explain code-generation success
hypotheses.result: Partially supported; function reachability shows strongest correlation, but causality unclear
